clinicalPearls: Causes horizontal binocular diplopia that is worse at distance and resolves or improves at near, the reverse of convergence insufficiency
There is a comitant esotropia greater for distance than near, with full abduction of each eye
It is most often a benign age-related condition sometimes called age-related distance esotropia
Abduction is full, which helps distinguish it from a sixth nerve palsy where abduction is limited
New-onset cases warrant exclusion of posterior fossa pathology and raised intracranial pressure
Prisms in spectacles usually relieve the distance diplopia effectively
reference.pathophysiology: Divergence insufficiency reflects an imbalance between convergence and divergence tone, with relatively reduced divergence producing an esodeviation that is greatest when the eyes should be parallel for distance viewing. In the common age-related form, degenerative changes in the orbital connective-tissue pulleys and extraocular muscle mechanics are thought to contribute. Because reduced divergence can also result from pontine or cerebellar disease and from raised intracranial pressure, a secondary neurological cause must be considered when onset is acute or accompanied by other signs.
additionalInvestigations: Orthoptic measurement of the deviation for distance and near
Assessment of abduction to exclude a sixth nerve palsy
MRI of the brain and posterior fossa in atypical or acute cases
Acetylcholine-receptor antibody testing if myasthenia is suspected
redFlags: Limited abduction indicating a sixth nerve palsy
Papilloedema or headache suggesting raised intracranial pressure
reference.prognosis: The benign age-related form is generally stable and responds well to prisms; prognosis in secondary cases depends on the underlying neurological cause.
pitfalls: Mistaking it for a bilateral sixth nerve palsy despite full abduction
Failing to exclude raised intracranial pressure in new-onset cases
Overlooking myasthenia as a fluctuating mimic
Assuming a benign cause without measuring distance and near deviations
references: Bradley and Daroff Neurology in Clinical Practice
management: Base-out prism correction in spectacles to relieve the distance binocular diplopia, the mainstay for the benign age-related form
Orthoptic review measuring the esodeviation for distance and near to guide prism strength
Exclude and treat a secondary neurological cause such as posterior fossa pathology or raised intracranial pressure in new-onset or atypical cases
Strabismus surgery for large or prism-intolerant deviations
Neuro-ophthalmology or neurology referral where a secondary cause is suspected
Periodic monitoring as the deviation may change over time
